newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU delay would boost mark - Buba's Welteke.
newsitem.headline: EMU delay would boost mark - Buba's Welteke.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Monday that any delay in European economic and monetary union (EMU) would have the negative effect of giving a sharp boost to the German mark.
In a speech prepared for delivery in the north German city of Kiel, Welteke also said there was no provision in the Maastricht Treaty for delaying the single currency launch.
"The collapse of the starting date could have negative consequences, particularly for Germany, as we would then have to expect a sharp rise in the mark," he said.
Welteke added that the recent fall in the mark was simply a correction of the over-appreciation seen in 1994/1995 and that the slide in the mark did not present a problem for the Bundesbank.

Looking ahead to the transition to the single European currency, Welteke said there were two main discussion plans on the table concerning the exchange rates at which national currencies should be transferred into the new euro.

Under the first plan, the current central rates used within the European Monetary System would be used as a basis for the transition, he said. In the second, average market rates over a period of e.g. two years would be taken, he said.
The first method would increase the need for currency market intervention and close policy coordination to ensure that exchange rates held steady, he noted.
But he said this nonetheless currently seemed a better option as it would force central banks to coordinate policy.
The single currency is due to be launched in 1999.
